experiment: collect direct calls during body lowering instead of a second Syn visitor pass
hypothesis: Fusing call-edge collection into the existing expression lowering walk should reduce front-end work while preserving the HIR call graph, including calls nested inside unsupported syntax.
measurement: Quill check-subset front-end only; not a Cargo build or rustc comparison.
measurement_method: Seven fresh processes before and after; Linux wait4 rusage for CPU and peak RSS; perf_counter wall time.
correctness_gate: The experimental version passed workspace tests, a focused unsupported/nested-call syntax test, and a byte-for-byte comparison of complete HIR/reachability output for the benchmark corpus.
decision: Reject and restore the original call collection pass. CPU changed by only -0.31%, wall time regressed by 0.44%, and RSS rose 0.20%; these differences are within run noise. Keep the independently measured source line-start index optimization.
